title: Surjectivity and kernel of the symmetric algebra map
statement: For a surjective linear map p : N → M, the induced symmetric algebra map is surjective and its ring-hom kernel is the ideal generated by the images of ker p.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DO (lemma-presentation-sym-exterior, line 2241; proof omitted in the source): for an exact sequence M_2 -> M_1 -> M -> 0 the sequences M_2 (x) Sym^{n-1}(M_1) -> Sym^n(M_1) -> Sym^n(M) -> 0 are exact. With M_1 = N, M_2 = K, the image of K (x) Sym^{n-1}(N) in Sym^n(N) is iota_N(K) * Sym^{n-1}(N), and the sum over n >= 1 of these is the ideal generated by iota_N(K); so the statement is 00DO summed over all degrees n (degree 0: Sym^0 = R on both sides)
